title: Count or Size? Two Weaknesses and a Synapse with No Packets

scenes.tts: Two diseases both make muscles weak. How can a recording tell them apart?
scenes.visual: Two muscle fibres side by side, each labelled weak, with the question on screen.
scenes.narration: Two diseases both make muscles weak. How can a recording tell them apart?

scenes.tts: Return to the rule. The response is roughly count times size.
scenes.caption: Return to the rule: response ≈ count × size.
scenes.visual: Card: response ≈ count × size.
scenes.narration: Return to the rule: response ≈ count × size.

scenes.tts: A muscle weakens when the response falls below what the fibre needs to fire.
scenes.visual: A train of response bars against a dashed threshold line. Label: illustrative threshold, 12 mV above rest.
scenes.narration: A muscle weakens when the response falls below what the fibre needs to fire.

scenes.tts: In myasthenia gravis, antibodies in most patients target the muscle's acetylcholine receptors.
scenes.visual: Antibodies bind receptors on the muscle membrane. Label: myasthenia gravis.
scenes.narration: In myasthenia gravis, antibodies in most patients target the muscle's acetylcholine receptors.

scenes.tts: Fewer receptors means a smaller packet size.
scenes.visual: The size factor on the card shrinks. Label: q down.
scenes.narration: Fewer receptors means a smaller packet size.

scenes.tts: An immunoglobulin fraction from patients' serum, moved into mice, gave them smaller miniatures and fewer receptors.
scenes.visual: A syringe moves from a patient-serum tube to a mouse; the mouse's miniatures shrink and its receptors thin out.
scenes.narration: An immunoglobulin fraction from patients' serum, moved into mice, gave them smaller miniatures and fewer receptors.

scenes.tts: Take the made-up junction, and suppose the first impulse releases exactly sixty packets. Cut the size, and that response still fires, but barely.
scenes.visual: The first bar of the myasthenic train sits just above the threshold line. Label: simple steady-state model, driving force 90 mV, threshold 12 mV above rest, fixed packet counts for illustration. Numbers on screen: k = 60 packets on this impulse, q = 0.24 mV, 14.4 mV by count × size, 12.4 mV by the balance point.
scenes.narration: Take the made-up junction, and suppose the first impulse releases exactly sixty packets. Cut the size, and that response still fires, but barely.

scenes.tts: But release runs down during repeated impulses, as ready vesicles get used up. Suppose a later impulse releases a quarter fewer packets.
scenes.visual: The trains run on; the bars get shorter. Label: k falls from 60 to 45 packets per impulse (fixed counts for illustration).
scenes.narration: But release runs down during repeated impulses, as ready vesicles get used up. Suppose a later impulse releases a quarter fewer packets.

scenes.tts: The normal fibre still fires. The myasthenic fibre drops below threshold and fails. Real counts also vary from impulse to impulse, so a response near threshold can fail even earlier.
scenes.visual: Normal train stays above the line (15.0 mV, model, 45 packets). Myasthenic train drops below it (9.6 mV, model, 45 packets) and the fibre stops twitching. Small note: real counts fluctuate around their average.
scenes.narration: The normal fibre still fires. The myasthenic fibre drops below threshold and fails. Real counts also vary from impulse to impulse, so a response near threshold can fail even earlier.

scenes.tts: This is fatigable weakness. Muscles work at first and weaken with use.
scenes.visual: Label: fatigable weakness.
scenes.narration: This is fatigable weakness. Muscles work at first and weaken with use.

scenes.tts: Drugs that block acetylcholinesterase let each packet's acetylcholine last longer.
scenes.visual: An acetylcholinesterase inhibitor is added; ACh lingers in the cleft.
scenes.narration: Drugs that block acetylcholinesterase let each packet's acetylcholine last longer.

scenes.tts: It reaches more of the remaining receptors. That raises the size part of the way back toward normal.
scenes.visual: The myasthenic bars grow taller, but not to full height. Label: q partly restored.
scenes.narration: It reaches more of the remaining receptors. That raises the size part of the way back toward normal.

scenes.tts: In Lambert-Eaton syndrome, the fault is in the terminal.
scenes.visual: The terminal highlights. Label: Lambert-Eaton syndrome.
scenes.narration: In Lambert-Eaton syndrome, the fault is in the terminal.

scenes.tts: Antibodies against its calcium channels cut calcium entry. So the count is low, while the size is normal.
scenes.visual: Antibodies block calcium channels. Short bars from the start, below the line. Numbers on screen: k = 20 packets per impulse, q = 0.40 mV (normal), about 7 to 8 mV (model).
scenes.narration: Antibodies against its calcium channels cut calcium entry. So the count is low, while the size is normal.

scenes.tts: Now stimulate rapidly, twenty times a second. What happens to the count during the train?
scenes.caption: Now stimulate rapidly, at 20 Hz. What happens to the count during the train?
scenes.visual: A fast train of stimuli at 20 Hz begins. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now stimulate rapidly, at 20 Hz. What happens to the count during the train?

scenes.tts: It rises. Calcium left over from one impulse adds to the next.
scenes.visual: Calcium builds up inside the terminal from impulse to impulse.
scenes.narration: It rises. Calcium left over from one impulse adds to the next.

scenes.tts: Because release rises steeply with calcium, a little extra calcium brings a large rise in the count.
scenes.visual: The bars grow during the train and climb toward the threshold line.
scenes.narration: Because release rises steeply with calcium, a little extra calcium brings a large rise in the count.

scenes.tts: Slow stimulation can instead give a decrement, a shrinking response. Calcium clears between impulses, and run-down wins.
scenes.visual: A slow train: calcium clears between impulses, and the bars shrink slightly.
scenes.narration: Slow stimulation can instead give a decrement, a shrinking response. Calcium clears between impulses, and run-down wins.

scenes.tts: So the two diseases leave opposite fingerprints.
scenes.visual: A two-row diagnostic table begins to draw.
scenes.narration: So the two diseases leave opposite fingerprints.

scenes.tts: A smaller size with a normal count points to the size side. That means receptors, or vesicle filling.
scenes.visual: Row: q down, m normal → size side (receptors, or vesicle filling). Small note under the table: assumes resting potential, membrane and recording site unchanged.
scenes.narration: A smaller size with a normal count points to the size side. That means receptors, or vesicle filling.

scenes.tts: A lower count with a normal size points to release from the terminal.
scenes.visual: Row: m down, q normal → count side (release from the terminal).
scenes.narration: A lower count with a normal size points to release from the terminal.

scenes.tts: One caution. Poorly filled vesicles also shrink the size. So pair the recording with a receptor count.
scenes.visual: A half-filled vesicle beside the size row. Label: pair with a receptor count.
scenes.narration: One caution. Poorly filled vesicles also shrink the size. So pair the recording with a receptor count.

scenes.tts: Finally, a synapse with no packets at all. At an electrical synapse, gap junctions join the two cells.
scenes.visual: Two cells joined by gap-junction channels. Label: electrical synapse.
scenes.narration: Finally, a synapse with no packets at all. At an electrical synapse, gap junctions join the two cells.

scenes.tts: Current passes directly, with no vesicles. So there is no quantal count or size, and no release failures.
scenes.visual: Current flows straight through the channels. Crossed-out labels: vesicle count, quantal size, release failures.
scenes.narration: Current passes directly, with no vesicles. So there is no quantal count or size, and no release failures.

scenes.tts: The coupled response still has a size. It can be too small to fire the next cell.
scenes.visual: A small depolarization crosses to the second cell and stays below its threshold line.
scenes.narration: The coupled response still has a size. It can be too small to fire the next cell.

scenes.tts: Most are very fast, and pass current both ways. Some rectify, passing current more easily one way.
scenes.visual: Arrows both ways through the junction; then one arrow thickens, labelled rectifying.
scenes.narration: Most are very fast, and pass current both ways. Some rectify, passing current more easily one way.

scenes.tts: At this chemical synapse, the response is roughly count times size. Ask which one moved, or both.
scenes.caption: At this junction, response ≈ count × size. Ask which one moved, or both.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: response ≈ count × size. Which one moved, or both?
scenes.narration: At this junction, response ≈ count × size. Ask which one moved, or both.
